title: Serious adverse event: late neurotropic disease associated with yellow fever vaccine.
ehr_evidence: The study is a single-patient case report based on clinical evaluation at Hospital Geral de Carapicuíba, São Paulo, Brazil; no electronic/computerised individual-level health database was analysed.
summary: A case report of a previously healthy 9-month-old male infant in São Paulo who developed late neurotropic disease (acute disseminated encephalomyelitis) 20 days after yellow fever vaccination, with full neurological recovery.
key_findings: The patient developed neurotropic disease associated with the yellow fever vaccine, confirmed by positive anti-yellow fever IgM antibodies in cerebrospinal fluid (risk of neurotropic disease after yellow fever vaccine reported as 1:8000).

All other causes of meningoencephalitis were excluded (negative bacterial cultures, negative Gram stain, undetectable herpes-virus PCR), and the patient achieved complete neurological recovery within 10 days of hospitalization.
Published literature reports a mean time of adverse reaction after yellow fever vaccine ranging between 7 and 27 days, and the patient's onset at 20 days fell within this expected range.
captured_features: Cerebrospinal fluid biochemistry and cell count (leukocytes, lymphocytes, proteins, glucose, lactate)
Bacterial antigen testing (LATEX) and Gram stain
No alterations on computed tomography of the skull
Anti-yellow fever IgM antibodies in cerebrospinal fluid
pathologies_diseases: Neurotropic disease associated with yellow fever vaccine
population: Single 9-month-old male infant, previously healthy, from the municipality of São Paulo, Brazil
limitations: Single patient case report, so no causal inference or generalizability is possible.
No control group and no quantitative effect estimates; relies on temporal association and exclusion of alternative diagnoses.
